title: There’s up to 50% off Criterion Collection 4K Blu-rays right now — here are my 9 picks from the sale, all of…
excerpt: There are tons of Criterion Collection 4K Blu-ray discs on sale — and I've picked 6 of my top recommendations.
content_html:
4K Blu-ray fans, it's back: The Criterion Collection sale is happening right now, with up to 50% off a large selection of 4K discs.

You can check out the full selection at The Criterion Channel page on Amazon US, but below, I've picked nine of my favorite discs from the sale, most of which have featured in our Blu-ray Bounty, where we test the latest 4K releases each month.

Hot off the presses, K-Pop Demon Hunters has only been a couple of weeks, but it's already discounted so there's no better time to pick one of 2025's biggest movies. Expect vivid and vibrant colors and a punchy Atmos soundtrack.

If you're looking for a showcase for 4K Blu-ray's capabilities, then check out Double Indemnity, Gilda, 3:10 To Yuma, Godzilla and 12 Angry Men. All of these are black-and-white movies that demonstrate superb contrast, showing a great balance between light, dark and gray tones. Each one of these has crisp textures on 4K, with the format breathing new life into these titles: one of its strengths.

Elsewhere, Frankenstein (2025) is another recent release that has gorgeous picture quality, with realistic textures, powerful contrast and an excellent Dolby Atmos soundtrack that will let your home theater flex its muscles.

Dead Man is another black-and-white title, albeit released in the 90s, that again shows staggering contrast, with deep black tones and fantastic brightness, especially during its daytime scenes.

Finally, The Breakfast Club looks great in 4K, with bold colors and sharp textures, showing once again what 4K can do for older movies. Close-up shots of characters really show how detailed 4K can be.

Before joining the team, he worked at a major UK based AV retailer selling TV and audio equipment, where he was either telling customers the difference between OLED and QLED or being wowed by watching a PS5 run on the LG 65G2. When not writing about the latest TV tech, James can be found gaming, reading, watching rugby or coming up with another idea for a novel.
